Route 2 : QC Hall - Litex/IBP Road
Route 3: Welcome Rotonda - Aurora Katipunan
Route 4: QC Hall - General Luis
Route 5: QC Hall - Mindanao Ave. via Visayas Ave. 
Route 6: QC Hall - Gilmore 
Route 7: QC Hall - C5/Ortigas Ave. Extension 
Route 8: QC Hall - Muñoz

Narito ang ruta at schedule ng biyahe ng Q City Bus: https://t.co/x7LtiZOceC

data.raw_text:
Martin sacrificed by Chito Fuentes (Part 1 of 2) 

Does President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. have what it takes to dump Speaker Martin Romualdez?

That was the question on everybody’s lips when talks first surfaced about the possibility of Romualdez stepping down as the undisputed ruler of the House of Representatives (HoR). The cynicism is understandable. At no time in the nation’s history has there been a Speaker feared by his peers, a reputation earned after his systematic demolition of those who dared cross his path.

While First Lady Liza Marcos gets much of the credit for most of BBM’s major decisions owing to his inherently weak and indecisive character, there is no argument that Romualdez casts a dark spell over the nation.

So when the possibility of finally getting rid of Romualdez surfaced in the aftermath of one of the worst floods to hit the National Capital Region (NCR), there were more doubters who said BBM does not have what it takes to take down his cousin. For a while, BBM validated that cynicism by resorting to PR blitzes that only to buried him deeper. 

It came as a surprise that after BBM’s mysterious trip to the US, he suddenly went on an ill-advised offensive to project himself as the graft buster that he never was. After visiting flood control projects that were overpriced and substandard one after another, his handlers realized that what they thought was the cure was in fact worse than the disease - they had to abort the blitz.  

Investigations were launched in both the Senate and the HoR obviously calculated to cool down the rising temperatures, to disastrous results. The revelations of Curlee and Sarah Dizcaya contained in sworn affidavits implicated Romualdez, Rep. Zaldy Co and other prominent solons, prompting BBM to push the panic button and unseat then Senate President Francis Escudero.

The HoR version desperately tried to cushion the blows inflicted on its members by the Dizcayas’ affidavits and countered with the testimonies of DPWH officials who implicated Senators Joel Villanueva and Jinggoy Estrada while a contractor identified with Escudero admitted he donated P30 million to the latter’s campaign kitty. It did not even disturb the waters.

Malacañang’s allies in the HoR, the yellows and pinks as well as the leftist Makabayan bloc attempted to muddle the issue by widening the scope of their investigation to include projects under the previous administration, but it only made them look ridiculous and pathetic. How can the projects of the Duterte administration have any bearing on the mangling of the 2024 and 2025 annual budgets? How does the flood control projects in Davao City have any bearing on the flooding in Metro Manila? If these are not ridiculous and pathetic, we don’t know what is.

 BBM tried a different tact: creating an independent commission to investigate the scams but few take it seriously. Its credibility has been questioned by Co even before it can be convened due to the statements issued by Baguio Mayor Benjamin Magalong that virtually alluded to the Bicol solon as the “mastermind” prior to the mayor’s appointment as its special adviser.

New DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon and the commission members hit the ground running, aware that they are racing against time but the problem is that few people take its independence seriously. BBM has his hands full just to keep his head above the water.
